clinical_diagnosis_summary: The patient presents with post-rotator cuff surgery pain in the shoulder and secondary neck pain due to prolonged sitting. This kinetic chain circuit addresses the primary shoulder dysfunction (Protocol 1) by restoring glenohumeral abduction, integrates scapulohumeral rhythm and proximal kinetic chain stability with bilateral overhead wall slides (Protocol 5), and anchors the circuit with axial postural control via cervical spine stabilization and ergonomic awareness (Protocol 3). This sequential approach aims to improve shoulder function while mitigating compensatory patterns originating from the cervical spine and scapulothoracic region.
precautions: Avoid compensatory scapular elevation during abduction (Protocol 1 & 5). Maintain pain-free range of motion, stopping if pain exceeds 4/10. Ensure controlled movement velocities, avoiding ballistic or rapid motions. Focus on smooth, coordinated movements throughout the circuit. Maintain neutral cervical spine alignment during all exercises, especially Protocol 5.

exercises.clinical_rationale: Directly addresses glenohumeral joint mobility and strength post-surgery, focusing on controlled abduction without excessive scapular elevation.

Enhances scapulohumeral rhythm and proximal kinetic chain integration, promoting coordinated movement between the shoulder girdle and thoracic spine, which can indirectly alleviate compensatory neck strain.

Establishes an axial postural anchor by reinforcing proper cervical spine alignment and engaging deep neck flexors, directly addressing the patient's reported neck pain and improving overall postural stability.
